scope: V1-V5 fixes, console-owner integration, explicit opt-in and the separate guest input launcher. No hardware, guest execution, source edits or physical-input claim. The earlier review is preserved.

closed_findings.result: feed refuses the existing expired deadline before consuming a READY or changing its deadline. Tests cover the boundary, a late READY and a fragmented READY finishing late.

Content-phase motion is parsed and checked against local (200,100), tolerance one pixel; contradictory or malformed motion clears a queued click. Same-chunk regression passes; later titlebar drag is not incorrectly subjected to the content-point constraint.

The bounded decimal grammar rejects malformed, nonfinite, signed-negative and excessively long coordinates before conversion. Accepted strings cannot make float conversion throw. Failure remains sticky.

Press evidence now requires a prior keying emission. Because the first keying action is fixed A-down, this establishes the intended causal ordering; integration write errors terminate the owner before further observations.
Upper endpoints are clamped to 32767; integer validation bounds the lower endpoints. Current interior schedule points are unchanged.

assessment: The same secondary-CDC owner calls feed/tick and writes returned bytes. Empty reads also advance time. There is no additional reader or timer-thread serial writer.

Attempted TX is recorded and fsynced before the serial write; short and exceptional writes enter the owner's sticky failure path and invalidate schedule completion, including failure on the final release.

close signals finish and joins before cancellation/reporting/device close. Unknown still-running ownership prevents successful finalization. No schedule retry or guessed SOH resynchronization is added.
Virtual input defaults off. Its exact version/origin/output/client/content-origin record is required alongside desktop opt-in and a hash-bound RAM root; keyboard mode is excluded.
The verified KC must contain PDSerialHID and IOHIDFamily and must exclude PDM1SPIHID. The guest framebuffer must match 2560x1600, stride 10240 and 30-bit depth before input execution.

Both controller and launcher pin the exact helper hash. The canonical desktop command remains fixed, single-use and nonce-validated; guest text cannot choose commands, coordinates, key usages or retry counts.
The corrected --run --socket PATH --input pdhid order matches the strict wm-darwin/src/main.rs parser.
Nonce is exactly 48 lowercase hex characters. Runtime directory is mode 0700. No human prompt, synthetic device node or user-provided command path is introduced.
The nonce PRIME barrier precedes stat-only character-device polling: at most 50 sleeps of 0.1 s, then a 0.5 s quiet delay. Both real nodes are required before --input pdhid is started.

The native sleep source supports fractional seconds. The compositor opens both real queues with nonblocking/no-follow/close-on-exec flags and drains its bounded pre-open backlog before advertising the seat.

The socket wait is bounded by 100 sleeps of 0.1 s and checks the owned compositor PID. The exact client-input binary is started with the fresh nonce and a 120-second bound; the script's nominal active interval is 100 seconds.
Cleanup signals and waits only for the stored child PIDs, client first then compositor. It does not force text-console painting while the compositor owns the framebuffer.
limits: The node check and quiet delay are ordering aids, not an acknowledgement that every prime was consumed. They do not qualify physical input or bypass the later actual READY/key/point/button/OBSERVED barriers.

The child wait calls are not individually timed. The enclosing host-worker/controller bounds remain necessary if guest teardown stalls. END alone is not clean PDGOP-close or console-restoration proof.
The client is normally terminated by the script before its 120-second normal completion. Do not claim client exit 0 or CLIENT_DONE from a successful input observation or END marker.

The packet assembler must place this reviewed script at the fixed /usr/bin/darwin-desktop-test path in the hash-bound RAM root, together with the exact client-input binary and XKB data. This review did not inspect or stage a new packet.

checks.includes: Root's new short/exceptional final-write regression, same-owner empty-read pacing and close cancellation.

checks.scope: Syntax only; script was not executed.

checks.result: Short return and OSError each produced exactly one attempted final release, sticky failure, schedule_completed=false, CLI proof false, preserved attempted TX and no subsequent write.
checks.scope: Directly seeded final-drag state exercises the real owner/error/finalization path, not full hardware execution.

remaining_evidence_boundary: No new source blocker was found in this bounded re-review.

schedule_completed describes completed host emissions only. Qualify host-origin input from the fresh client's exact events plus the successful ordered TX ledger; qualify window dragging from actual resulting geometry/framebuffer evidence.
A controller command-line verdict remains a command-line verdict. It cannot by itself prove Wayland input, drag, compositor cleanup, panel scanout or physical keyboard/trackpad support.
The root-owned live boot uses its archived older sources. These local revisions must not be attributed to that run.
